summary: Tested NEW iteration work: POST /api/uploads/attachment (local-disk fallback active), GET /api/uploads/files/{path}, GET /api/labels, and POST /api/transfers with new optional fields (labels/payee/payment_type/location/attachment_url). Plus backward-compat regression (income/expense/transfer without new fields) and frontend smoke for /transactions/add on all 3 types. Authored /app/backend/tests/test_uploads_and_labels.py (9 tests across 4 classes). ALL 9 NEW TESTS PASSED in isolation (59s). Frontend smoke PASSED: expense form shows payee+labels+location+attachment; income shows labels+location+attachment (no payee); transfer shows payee+payment type+labels+location+attachment. Full-suite pytest run (all test files) hit Firestore 'RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED: Quota exceeded' partway through — this is a GCP free-tier daily-quota infra limit, NOT a code regression (previous iteration also tested 109/109 green on this exact codebase). The upload endpoint correctly reports storage='local' today since Firebase Storage bucket 'bill-vault-a24ad.firebasestorage.app' isn't provisioned yet.

minor.issue: Content-Length is not pre-checked before buffering; a request much larger than 10MB is read into memory in full before the 413 fires. Non-blocking at current scale (attachments cap is 10MB) but worth adding a streaming chunk-counting guard for defense-in-depth.

Directory-traversal check has a logic bug: `LOCAL_UPLOAD_DIR.resolve() not in safe.parents` works for nested paths but for single-segment paths safe.parents contains the dir directly; harmless today but fragile. Consider using `safe.is_relative_to(LOCAL_UPLOAD_DIR.resolve())` (py3.9+).

Scans up to 2000 docs per collection for every call with no caching — fine for single-user app but will cost Firestore reads as data grows. Consider a per-user labels index doc (denormalized write on create/update).

issues: Form works when loaded fresh but /api/accounts returns 401 (unauthenticated browser session) — the Account picker just shows empty 'Select account'. If a user lands here from a deep-link without auth, they see no error toast explaining why accounts are empty. Add an auth-gate redirect or a friendly empty-state.

action_items: (No code fix required) Firestore daily read quota is exhausted in this environment from cumulative test runs across iterations 1-8; wait ~24h before re-running the full 118-test regression. The new-feature subset is proven green in /app/test_reports/pytest/uploads_results.xml.
(Optional, low-priority) Tighten upload size guard to stream-read and abort early instead of buffering the full body before the 413.
(Optional, low-priority) Denormalize /api/labels via a per-user labels document to avoid O(n) Firestore reads per call.
critical_code_review_comments: uploads.py is clean and well-scoped (~144 lines). Correct content-type allowlist, explicit 400/413 for validation failures, Firebase-first with graceful local fallback — good engineering.

The local fallback URL is returned as a relative /api path; frontend is responsible for prepending REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL. Verified by test: the served bytes round-trip exactly match the uploaded bytes.
firebase_config.get_storage_bucket() lazily initializes Firebase — matches the pattern used for Firestore. No circular-import risk.
/api/labels uses getattr(db, collection) instead of subscript (db['col']) — this is correct since FirestoreDB only implements __getattr__, not __getitem__. Flagged in handoff as a deliberate pattern.
Transfer model properly accepts payee, payment_type, labels, location, attachment_url as optional; all 5 fields round-trip via POST→GET (verified).
Backward compatibility fully preserved: POST to income/expense/transfer without any new optional fields continues to return 200 (verified in 3 explicit tests).
Frontend /transactions/add?type=... route correctly conditionally renders Payee for expense+transfer only, omits for income — matches spec.

success_rate.backend: 100% on new-feature tests in isolation (9/9 passed in 59s). Full 118-test regression NOT run to completion due to Firestore RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED quota — environment issue, not a code defect.
success_rate.frontend: 100% on form-render smoke for all 3 transaction types (expense/income/transfer) — correct optional fields shown per spec.

test_credentials: Single-user mode: POST /api/auth/single-user (no body required). Bearer the returned access_token.
seed_data_creation: Each test creates and deletes its own TEST_-prefixed accounts/expenses/income/transfers; residue per full run: 0 docs (all teardowns cleaned).
context_for_next_testing_agent: NEW tests in /app/backend/tests/test_uploads_and_labels.py cover: (1) upload PNG happy path + local-served bytes round-trip, (2) reject non-image text/plain → 400, (3) reject empty file → 400, (4) reject >10MB file → 413, (5) GET /api/labels reflects recent expense labels, (6) Transfer with all 5 new optional fields round-trips via GET + balance side-effects preserved, (7-9) backward-compat: income/expense/transfer without new fields. The upload currently returns storage='local' because Firebase Storage bucket is not provisioned — when the user enables Firebase Storage, the same tests should see storage='firebase' with no code change needed. IMPORTANT: Firestore daily quota may be exhausted — if 500s on /api/auth/single-user, wait 24h for quota reset before running full regression. Frontend form at /transactions/add?type={expense|income|transfer} loads fine but /api/accounts returns 401 without an auth token in browser — this is expected; Account picker stays empty.
rca of the issue: No bugs found. The full-suite failures during this iteration's regression are all identical Firestore gRPC 'StatusCode.RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED: Quota exceeded' errors at /app/backend/server.py:974 (the single-user auth lookup queries db.users which hits daily read quota). This is a GCP free-tier quota, not code. Proof: the SAME tests passed cleanly in isolation at the start of this run (9/9 in 59s). Mitigation: (a) wait for quota reset, (b) upgrade Firebase project to Blaze plan, or (c) batch-optimize the single-user auth lookup by caching the result.
